iqa2lh6i4tkh3gje892fsvl062.value: Credits: deterministic lockstep, where only inputs travel and every machine works out the same state, is from Mark Terrano and Paul Bettner, "1500 Archers on a 28.8" (Age of Empires, GDC 2001) (prior art). The cart on a spring, the page and Fixed are ours.

jarh477ouc6ujan5o0r69p9a7f.value: In a networked game, two machines don't send each other the game. They send only what each player pressed, and each machine works the game out for itself. That works only if both get exactly the same numbers from the same presses, to the last bit. Float64 doesn't promise that: different processors and compilers can round the last bit differently, and a tiny difference grows. So this cart is worked out in Fixed, numbers kept as whole steps of 2⁻³², which every machine adds and multiplies the same way.
